requestedActions.title: List active task titles for the connected Todoist account, including pagination

guide.summary: Todoist documents user-authorized OAuth2 (authorization code flow) for external apps, so customers can connect individual accounts. Developers must first register an app in the App Management Console with redirect URLs to obtain a Client ID and Client Secret. The active-task listing endpoint (GET /api/v1/tasks) is cursor-paginated. The read-only scope covering it is not identified in citable passages: the data:read definition is non-citable, so the action stays unresolved. Distribution, review and customer-admin approval policy are unknown.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List active task titles for the connected Todoist account, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Todoist documents user-authorized OAuth2 authorization code flow
findings.detail: Apps obtain a user-authorized API token via OAuth2. The authorization request uses client_id, state and optional response_type code, with an optional redirect_uri. The token is then exchanged at the access_token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and code.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their individual Todoist accounts

evidence.quote: external applications to obtain a user authorized API token via the OAuth2
https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Once you have the authorization code , you can exchange it for the access token

steps.title: Send test user to Todoist consent and verify the callback
steps.detail: Redirect a test user to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, a unique unguessable state, scope and response_type=code. The user approves the app. The callback must return the same state value before the code is accepted. The scope must be a read scope confirmed for the task-listing operation; the snapshot leaves the exact read-only scope unresolved, so this URL is a template with a placeholder scope.
steps.doneWhen: Callback query contains code and the returned state exactly matches the value generated for this request.

client_id The unique Client ID of the Todoist application that you registered.
A unique and unguessable string. It is used to protect you against cross-site request forgery attacks.

fields: CLIENT_ID: from app registration
READ_SCOPE_CONFIRMED: read scope to be confirmed; not identified in citable passages
RANDOM_STATE: unguessable value generated per request

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for access token
steps.detail: After the callback check passes, POST the code to the documented token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and the code from the callback. This is an unexecuted authorization step. The response contains access_token used for later read requests.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 response includes access_token and token_type Bearer; access token is stored for the test session only.

steps.title: Request first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with an OAuth access token and limit=50 to fetch the first page of active tasks. Read each result's content property as the task title and record next_cursor from the response. Boundary check: confirm the granted scope is read-only and issue no write, complete or delete request.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with a results array; each result's content value is captured as a task title; next_cursor is recorded as a string or null.

evidence.quote: Get Tasks Get all active tasks for the user.
{ "id" : "..." , "content" : "..." , "priority" : 4 }

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access_token from the token exchange response
limit: page size chosen as 50

steps.title: Request next page of active tasks using next_cursor
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor set to the previous next_cursor value, the same limit and the same token, then read content from each result as a task title. Keep requesting pages until next_cursor is null, which is the documented end of results. Boundary check: issue only GET requests; make no task write or completion call.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched in sequence until next_cursor is null; task titles from every page are captured.
